why: issue 2018 / RFC-0108 As-built -- the registering preemption level's own sched context, lowered from its tier policy: what the level's setup registers binds to it instead of the executor's default, which every level on the core shares, so a level's budget is charged to that level alone. rclcpp and rclrs have neither sched contexts nor preemption levels on one executor. See `rust:Executor::set_registering_level`.
